items.heading: These Sit on Top
items.text: These sit on top of the general questions worth asking any counselling provider, who actually counsels you, whether pricing is transparent, whether outcomes are framed honestly. For a student, four more things separate a genuinely good fit from a process that just happens to also serve students.

items.heading: These Are on Top
items.text: These are on top of the general red flags worth checking for any provider, undisclosed pricing, one-size-fits-all recommendations, guaranteed outcomes. These four are specific to whether a process was actually built with a student's situation in mind.

items.heading: Not Every Provider Adds
items.text: Not every provider adds the same thing once the four checks above hold up. This is the difference they point to.

items.heading: A Student's Decision Usually Involves
items.text: A student's decision usually involves a second stakeholder in the room: a parent or family member with their own concerns about cost, safety, and long-term outcomes. How that gets handled matters as much as the counselling content itself.

items.heading: "Follow Your Passion" Is Not
items.text: "Follow your passion" is not stream-specific credibility. A process that can name real trade-offs between your exact options is doing more work than one offering broad reassurance.

items.heading: No Honest Provider, Including This
items.text: No honest provider, including this one, can guarantee an admission outcome, a rank, or a placement. Treat that promise as a warning sign, not a selling point.
